replies.author: @peterstewart3806
replies.text:
@kevindahlenburg6014well for example, I run a business.  I hold back 25% of the income it generates all year but when tax time comes around and I go over the cost of running the business (with receipts) and depreciate the assets related to the business (ie the building and everything used related to the business), along with other expenses like insurance and property taxes (those are some of the big bills of the year) it looks on paper like I ran the business at a loss.  I end up oweing the government zero but I still have the 25% I held back in case I did need to pay taxes like I would have if I didn’t file my taxes at a loss.
And I’m just a couple of years I end up owning the building that I’ve “depreciated to zero” according to how I’ve done my taxes so it’s like getting a free piece of property.
